newsitem.title: UK: NWE fuel oil barges up $1 but prompt sellers weigh.
newsitem.headline: NWE fuel oil barges up $1 but prompt sellers weigh.

text.p: NWE fuel edged up $1 a tonne in early trading but aggressive selling on prompt barges pulled levels 50 cents back down towards lunchtime.
High sulphur barges traded from $82.50 up to $84 in Rotterdam before easing back when a prompt seller offered back down to $82.75.
But that seller was "just trying to move a blended Russian cargo, the rest of the market is well supported," said a trader.
Cargoes were discounted to barges and still talked $81 cif after trading at that level on Tuesday for delivery into Ireland.
Low sulphur cargoes were well supported around $94.50 fob NWE with July swaps talking some $2 lower.
Dealers said Italian demand remained subdued but narrow spreads against high sulphur were lending support.
"The low sulphur market is just trading off high-low spreads and straight-run," said a trader.
